newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Aug PPI rose 0.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- U.S. Aug PPI rose 0.3 pct.

text.p: Following are comments from U.S. economists after the Labor Department reported the August Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 0.3 percent, while the core index fell 0.1 percent.
Economists in a Reuters poll had expected a 0.1-percent rise in both the overall and core rates.
JAMES GLASSMAN, SENIOR MONEY MARKET ECONOMIST, CHASE SECURITIES INC: "I think it's neutral right now for the markets. We have to see retail sales tomorrow and (the Consumer Price Index)."
Glassman was speaking on Reuters Financial Television.

DAVID SLOAN, SENIOR ECONOMIST, I.D.E.A. INC: "It's a decent number. The strength in food prices is a bit unexpected but the core PPI rate is very subdued. The rise in energy prices was expected. The rise in food was a bit of a surprise.

"Prices at the crude and intermediate stages of production don't provide much strength. We've actually seen a fall in food prices at the crude level so the increase in food prices probably will not be sustained. The energy prices will be sustained due to the situation in Iraq."

Sloan went on: "The core rates are excellent. Overall, it's quite a comforting figure for the inflation outlook. As for the rise in jobless claims, we had a big fall last week and a rise this week. It's best to see the two weeks together. I wouldn't read too much into it.
"The Labor Day holiday fell in this reporting week. It shows that the labor market is still strong."
MARIA FIORINI RAMIREZ, PRESIDENT, MFR INC: "If we don't drive and we don't eat, we're okay. The report looks pretty decent. Overall PPI is up 2.1 percent year-to-date.

"For all of 1995 we were up 2.3. The core is up 0.5 percent against 2.6. Inflation numbers continue to be as benign as we had expected them to be. There are still inflation fears lurking out there on the wage side, but that's not the story this number tells you.
"Even though increases in gas prices or food prices are passed on pretty fast, from these numbers it looks like it won't be a problem for at least a couple of months."

CARY LEAHEY, SENIOR FINANCIAL MARKETS ECONOMIST, LEHMAN GOVERNMENT SECURITIES INC: "The number is favorable. Even though you had a higher headline print, the core rate was actually down and the (Treasury) market likes that.
"If there is a negative in the report, it's that if you look at the trend on core intermediate prices, which is a good leading indicator of inflation ... it appears to be bottoming.
"The market would say: 'If it's bottoming and it starts to turn around, will inflation follow six months from now?'That's the negative. It's going to raise a few eyebrows.
"You also got a big increase in food prices. The markets discount that ... the (Treasury) market really cares about the core rate and that has actually been declining so far this year."
